changes.after: JSON is text that represents data. Valid JSON can still contain the wrong kind of value for your program.

before: require "json" loads the available JSON library. JSON.parse returns Ruby values: an object normally becomes a Hash with string keys, while arrays, numbers and null produce other shapes. Valid JSON alone is not a valid study entry.

is_a?(Class) checks whether a value belongs to that class or a subclass. Range#cover? tests whether a value lies within its endpoints, inclusive for 1..60. Check the container, Integer type and range before use. JSON::ParserError is a syntax failure and is handled separately. The example uses fixed tiny input; external input also needs a size limit and an appropriate nesting policy. Do not replace JSON parsing with eval or unsafe object deserialization.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
require "json"
begin
  entry = JSON.parse('{"minutes":15}')
  value = entry.is_a?(Hash) ? entry["minutes"] : nil
  if value.is_a?(Integer) && (1..60).cover?(value)
    puts value
  else
    puts "invalid shape"
  end
rescue JSON::ParserError
  puts "invalid JSON"
end

```
Expected output or behavior: 15. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
